bug_semantics: A post-authenticated user with Create and Modify permission can write attacker-controlled bytes outside the user's scope when an in-scope symlink points to a not-yet-existing out-of-scope file. EvalSymlinks on the link returns fs.ErrNotExist; the guard then walks the lexical path up to the link's in-scope containing directory and approves that ancestor. The subsequent OpenFile call uses O_CREATE|O_TRUNC, so the OS follows the dangling symlink and creates the target outside the scope.
flaw_origin: Commit 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b introduced files.WithinScope and put it on the HTTP write path as an incomplete fix for an earlier symlink escape. Its new ErrNotExist fallback validated the nearest lexical existing ancestor and its own comment explicitly accepted dangling symlinks as best-effort. Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moved the same flawed fallback into ScopedFs.within and centralized OpenFile behind that guard; the refactor preserved rather than originated the flaw.
ai_marker: BIC commit object contains the exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Its author and committer are both Henrique Dias <mail@hacdias.com>; no bot identity is used. The commit-object co-author trailer is the attribution signal used for this verdict.
evidence: The first-party GitHub advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-8wc8-hf36-mjh9 identifies files/scoped.go, the dangling-symlink ErrNotExist walk-up, the POST /api/resources/<link>?override=true path, affected versions <= 2.63.15, first patched version 2.63.16, and fix commit 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

`git show 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b -- files/file.go http/resource.go` shows the BIC newly adding WithinScope, including `for errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)` followed by `parent := filepath.Dir(target)`, and newly calling it from writeFile before OpenFile. The added comment says a dangling symlink is allowed and creation callers should treat the check as best-effort.

`git log -L ':WithinScope:files/file.go' 3406d3d7f98dfc3c16e4ff7ff4a87e3bdfe221dd` traces the function's creation to 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b. `git log -S'dangling symlink whose target does not yet exist' -- files/file.go files/scoped.go` returns the BIC, the later move 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3, and the fix 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

Direct parent-tree verification: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` gives sole parent 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d, and `git grep -n -e WithinScope -e EvalSymlinks 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d -- '*.go'` returns no matches. The BIC diff is therefore the first parent-to-child appearance of the flawed guard.

`git show 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 -- files/file.go files/scoped.go http/resource.go users/users.go` shows a refactor deleting WithinScope and creating ScopedFs.within with the same ErrNotExist lexical-parent loop and dangling-symlink best-effort comment; ScopedFs.OpenFile guards and then delegates to BasePathFs.OpenFile.

At vulnerable release commit be23ab3a15bf957928ecfed88de5ab67850c1b9c (tag v2.63.15), http/resource.go resourcePostHandler requires Create, treats the dangling link as an existing entry and requires override=true plus Modify, then writeFile calls `afs.OpenFile(dst, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, ...)`. files/scoped.go OpenFile first calls the flawed guard and then delegates to s.base.OpenFile, which follows the link.

`git show 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 -- files/scoped.go` shows the direct fix: on ErrNotExist it Lstats the current target, detects a symlink, Readlinks and resolves it (including real-directory resolution for relative links), and validates the destination rather than the lexical parent. The same commit adds file-level and HTTP regression tests that reject a dangling escaping symlink and assert no outside file is created.

Version-boundary checks: `git tag --contains 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.6 and includes v2.63.15; `git tag --contains 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.16 and excludes v2.63.15. The v2.63.16 first-party release notes at https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases/tag/v2.63.16 list 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

`git cat-file commit 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` supplies the BIC-only AI evidence: human author/committer Henrique Dias and exact commit-message trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The commit is a one-parent direct commit in the public graph; GitHub's commit-to-pulls endpoint returns no associated PR, so there are no reconstructable squash member SHAs to substitute for it.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the incomplete confinement logic itself, not the later placement of that logic. The BIC added a guard intended to make symlink-backed reads and writes safe, but for a nonexistent target it discarded the unresolved leaf and approved the nearest existing lexical ancestor. A dangling final symlink is exactly the case where this inference is false: its parent is in scope while the eventual O_CREATE destination is outside. The write call was guarded by this new function in the same BIC, establishing causal content linkage. The immediate parent contains neither WithinScope nor any EvalSymlinks-based equivalent, while line-history and string-history identify 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b as the first writer. The later 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 commit is excluded as a BIC because it is a refactor that moves the unchanged faulty mechanism into ScopedFs. The advisory fix 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 directly resolves dangling links before deciding scope and lands in the first patched tag v2.63.16. Because the real BIC commit object explicitly co-authors Claude Opus 4.8 and that same commit first writes the causally flawed fallback and its write-path use, the appropriate closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
